scope: Corollary 7.10 (Order of finite choices) of the manuscript “Purely cosmetic surgery on knots in the three-sphere” (preprints/Purely-Cosmetic-Surgery-on-Knots-in-the-Three-Sphere-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 306 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ee916c92b825a868), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 92. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The constants CW can be fixed before choosing the delays, exceptional evaluations and repetition count in the stack. After those choices have specified a finite problem P, there are ϵ > 0, admissible finite auxiliary sizes, numbers δ > 0 and T0 < ∞, with the following property. For every collection of finite Y lengths Tj ≥ T0 and ordinary Floer- gradient perturbations of size at most δ, there is a positive allowed size for the further non-gradient perturbations such that all conclusions of Theorem 7.1 hold. The further size may depend on the chosen finite Tj; it includes their total squared error costs. At genuine ends the perturbations and backgrounds obey the product rule and the specified decreasing tail bounds.
